## Primary independently reviewable outcome

Produce an evidence-backed audit of the production Ridge MMM statistical specification and its
level-scale semantics, from panel DGP through fitted log mean, residual assumptions,
retransformation, aggregation, replay/calibration, full-panel Δmu, economics/ROI, and optimization.
The audit must derive behavior from source, compare candidate nuisance/media structures in
research-only evidence, identify current semantic limitations, and recommend independently
reviewable successor milestones. It must not change production analytical behavior.

## Atomic boundary

The audit report plus its machine-readable empirical evidence, if generated, are one research
evidence outcome. No production implementation, gate change, model promotion, contract change, or
decision-surface change is part of this task. Any correction method, new production specification,
retransformation policy, geo-varying coefficient implementation, or optimizer/economics change is a
separate successor requiring its own authorization.

## Required audit questions and evidence

1. **Current production model.** Derive Ridge directly from implementation: target transform,
   intercept, media transforms, controls, geo/week treatment, pooling, coefficient dimensions,
   residual assumptions, and inverse-transform prediction. State whether the implementation matches
   `log(Y_gt)=alpha+sum_c beta_c f_c(X_gtc)+gamma'Z_gt+error_gt`, or document the difference. Describe
   Bayesian only as a comparator and do not promote its authority.
2. **Panel mean structure.** Evaluate the implications of the current global intercept under geo
   baselines, common demand, trend, seasonality, holidays/shocks, and geo-specific shocks. Compare
   global intercept; geo effects with pooled betas; geo plus structured time baseline; geo plus
   saturated week effects; and regularized geo effects. Compare saturated weeks with trend, spline,
   Fourier, and known-event controls. Do not choose by predictive RMSE alone.
3. **Media-effect heterogeneity.** Distinguish pooled beta, regularized geo-varying beta, time-varying
   effects, and geo-time-varying effects. Assess identifiability, sample needs, stability, causal
   recovery, and overfit risk. Do not implement geo-varying production coefficients.
4. **National-channel identification.** For representative/synthetic channels quantify within-week
   cross-geo identifying variation, including `Var(X_gtc-mean_g(X_gtc))/Var(X_gtc)` and rank/
   conditioning diagnostics. Demonstrate strongly geo-varying, mixed, nearly national, and exactly
   national cases; show when saturated week effects destroy identification and what assumptions make
   structured time controls estimable. Do not weaken confounding controls to obtain coefficients.
5. **Log-to-level retransformation.** Trace every production log prediction and exponentiation. Compare
   plain `exp(mu)`, normal/lognormal `exp(mu+sigma^2/2)` where justified, Duan smearing, and
   conditional/geo smearing only diagnostically. Do not estimate a correction from residuals that
   still contain omitted geo/time structure and call it noise correction. State what each estimates.
6. **Aggregation order.** Trace every canonical path and confirm or reject whether any path uses
   `exp(mean(mu))` instead of `mean(exp(mu))`. Separate canonical planning/replay from legacy,
   diagnostic, decomposition, export, economics, and reporting paths. Preserve only findings proven
   by code.
7. **Delta-mu versus level economics.** Keep full-panel Delta-mu canonical. Empirically compare plan/channel
   rankings, optimizer allocations, hurdle/ROI decisions, and heteroskedastic sensitivity against
   corrected expected level deltas. Report whether any divergence is material; do not change the
   decision surface.
8. **Replay/calibration.** Trace inverse-transform semantics through replay and measure effects of
   omitted geo/time baselines, retransformation bias, aggregation mismatch, and media misspecification.
   Keep CalibrationSignal and experiment semantics unchanged.
9. **Synthetic truth.** Use existing H6/synthetic infrastructure where possible, verify its DGP source
   structures before relying on it, and use only research-only deterministic extensions if existing
   worlds are insufficient. Measure log error, level calibration and per-geo bias, effect recovery,
   Delta-mu and expected-level deltas, replay lift, national identification, ranking, and allocation;
   separate prediction from causal/decision recovery.
10. **Prior-validation blind spots.** Trace existing audits and H6 acceptance criteria. Distinguish
    what tested implementation/predictive/average coefficient recovery from what did not test geo
    baselines, time nuisance structure, retransformation, expected-level KPI recovery, nuisance
    sensitivity, or Delta-mu-level decision invariance.

## Required conclusions

Recommend later milestones for: canonical geo baselines; time-baseline family; pooled versus
regularized geo-varying effects; national-channel identifiability policy; residual/noise diagnostics;
retransformation and artifact semantics; aggregation semantics; replay implications; whether full-
panel Delta-mu remains sufficiently decision-equivalent; and synthetic certification additions.
Classify each recommendation as `supported_for_implementation`, `requires_more_evidence`, `rejected`,
or `research_only`. Split recommendations into independently reviewable successors and do not
implement them here.
